**Record of the Text**

The text is about a group of settlers who lived at a bend in a creek. Before the first snow of the season fell, these settlers had already finished building a sod house.

At some point, a message arrived from the railway agent who was located at the county seat. In this message, the agent promised to provide a carload of coal, but only on the condition that the neighbors in the area would subscribe to it together—that is, jointly agree to it as a group. The settlers' reply to this message was sent back within the same week that the message had arrived.

The winter that followed turned out to be a long one, though it was quiet. During that winter, the amount of fodder the settlers had on hand proved to be just sufficient—exactly enough to meet their needs, neither running short nor leaving a surplus.
